_comment: One reading per rule-carrying item: the item's title and check copied literally, the
verdict, the reading, and an answer for every shape tools/audit_item_readings.py detects.
Edited by hand only. A copy that no longer matches the registry is a pair nobody has re-read.

CI-001.title: Ensure URL Is Indexed

entry_answer.why: The item asks whether anything on the page or server stops Google from indexing it, and the status is one of those things: an entry answering 4xx or 5xx is not indexable, which the gate already measured.

CI-001.reading: The title asks whether the URL is indexed, which only Google knows; `rows` carries indexability_matrix's verdict, which lists what would stop indexing — robots.txt, status, noindex in meta or header, a canonical elsewhere. CI-002 asks Google. On an entry the audit could not read, `entry_answer` lets the entry's own request decide it: a 4xx or 5xx answer fails it, anything else is NO_DATA.

shapes.external: Indexing is Search Console's to report; this rule reads the page's own blockers, and `measures` says so.

CI-002.title: Confirm Google Has Indexed the Audited URL
CI-002.reading: `indexed` is URL Inspection's own coverage verdict for the audited URL, from Search Console.

CI-003.title: Page Returns 200 (OK) Status Code

entry_answer.why: The item asks what the audited page answers, and the entry gate stops the run on exactly the answers that fail it. Without this it could not fail in any finished audit (measured 30.09.2026).

CI-003.reading: `rows.0.status_class` classifies the audited URL's final status as Google's HTTP-status page reads it: 200 passes, another success warns, no content, a redirect that ends there, 4xx and 5xx fail. It is the audited page only; `measures` names CI-015 and GO-138 for the rest of the site. On an entry the audit could not read, `entry_answer` lets the entry's own request decide it: a 4xx or 5xx answer fails it, anything else is NO_DATA.

shapes.conjunction: The parenthetical is the status name, not a second subject.

CI-004.title: Allow Indexing via Meta Robots
CI-004.reading: `meta_robots` is every robots meta's content, joined (`None` when the page has none); the rule fails `noindex` in any case and `none` standing as a rule of its own, never `max-image-preview: none`'s argument, and passes a page without the tag (F15: the last tag alone was read, and case and `none` were not).

shapes.external: The word is *Indexing*, but the title's subject is the meta tag, which the page itself carries; no search engine data is needed.

second_reading.dispute: `parse_html()` overwrites `meta_robots` for each matching tag, so the asserted value contains only the last tag's content, not every directive. Testing that value for `noindex` can miss an earlier restrictive tag or the restrictive `none` directive, contradicting the claim that PASS means no directive disallows indexing.

CI-005.title: Do Not Block the URL in robots.txt
CI-005.reading: `rows.0.robots_allowed` is the RFC 9309 answer for Googlebot on the entry URL, from lib/robots_rules.

CI-006.title: Declare Sitemap Location in robots.txt
CI-006.reading: `sitemaps` lists the Sitemap: lines robots.txt declares; one is what the title asks.

shapes.existential: The title asks that the location be declared; one declaration satisfies it.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and existential answer mistake a counted directive for a declared location: `robots_rules.parse()` appends even an empty or arbitrary `Sitemap:` value, and `_parse_robots()` copies it into `sitemaps`. Thus `len_gte: 1` can pass without any sitemap location being declared; my verdict remains `owed`.

CI-008.title: Make the URL Discoverable via Internal Links/Navigation
CI-008.reading: `orphan_pages.count` is sitemap URLs the crawl found no internal link to, robots refusals excluded.

shapes.conjunction: Links/Navigation names one subject: an inbound internal link, navigation included.

second_reading.dispute: The reading incorrectly limits `orphan_pages.count` to sitemap URLs: `graph_from_inventory()` sets `crawled = set(pages)`, and `analyze_link_profile()` checks that entire set, with exclusions. I disagree with `answers` because `graph_from_inventory()` unconditionally credits the entry and its redirect destination, while `analyze_link_profile()` also exempts the entry, allowing PASS when the audited URL has no inbound internal link.

CI-009.title: Serve Content at a Single Canonical URL
CI-009.reading: `rows` maps canonical_checker's `verdict` with the target and the URL variants requested: a missing, conflicting or cross-host canonical, a target not answering 200, or a variant serving the page unconsolidated fails (F15). Other duplicate URLs are not requested, and `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict confuses a canonical declaration with serving content at a single canonical URL. `check_canonicals()` accepts `self_canonical` and same-host `canonicalized` without comparing content across URLs, and these arguments leave `check_targets=False`, allowing even a broken canonical target to pass.

CI-010.title: Align Google-Selected and Declared Canonical
CI-010.reading: `canonical_match` compares URL Inspection's Google-selected canonical with the declared one.

shapes.conjunction: Google-selected and Declared are the two sides of the one comparison the rule makes.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overlooks that `analyze()` computes `canonical_match` using `gc.rstrip("/") == uc.rstrip("/")`. Different canonical URLs such as `/page` and `/page/` therefore pass, although they can identify distinct resources; no measures sentence covers that gap.

CI-011.title: Avoid Canonical/Indexing Mixed Signals
CI-011.reading: `rows` maps canonical_checker's `signal`, read off the page's noindex and its canonical's fetched target together: two canonicals that disagree, noindex beside a canonical naming another URL, or a canonical naming a noindex page fails; a cross-host canonical alone is consistent (F15).

shapes.conjunction: Canonical/Indexing names the conflict between the two: noindex beside a canonical elsewhere, a canonical naming a page kept out of the index, and two canonicals that disagree.
shapes.external: The page's own signals are the subject, not Google's index.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and conjunction answer treat a cross-host canonical as inherently contradictory, although naming another host does not itself establish conflicting signals. `check_canonicals()` assigns `cross_host` solely from `same_host()`, while a same-host canonical can receive `consistent` without checking whether its target declares noindex. The external answer correctly distinguishes declared signals from Google's index, but does not resolve these gaps.

CI-012.title: Use a Friendly URL Structure
CI-012.reading: `rows.0.score` is 100 less 12 per url_quality flag; 70 allows two flags.

second_reading.dispute: The score computation is described correctly, but the `answers` verdict is unsupported: `max(0, 100 - 12 * len(flags))` permits any two flags, including `long_url` together with `deep_path`. That flag budget does not establish a friendly URL structure, and no measures sentence covers the gap.

CI-013.title: Do Not Block Critical CSS/JS/Images in robots.txt
CI-013.reading: `blocked_urls` lists same-origin CSS, JS and image URLs the page references that robots.txt blocks for Googlebot.

shapes.conjunction: CSS/JS/Images is one class of resource, all three read.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `discover_asset_paths()` reads explicit HTML references but neither identifies critical resources nor discovers CSS imports or CSS image references. Consequently, `blocked_urls` can fail over a noncritical resource or remain empty while a critical resource referenced through CSS is blocked; the conjunction answer does not resolve that gap.

CI-014.title: Use Correct Redirect Codes (No Chains/Loops)
CI-014.reading: `redirect_issues` fails a loop, a missing Location or a chain past Google's 10-hop limit, and warns on any chain or 302/303/307 (0.112.0).

shapes.conjunction: Codes, chains and loops are each an issue type the rule reads.
shapes.qualifier: *Correct* is read as permanent codes: a temporary code warns, since Google treats it as a weak signal.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and qualifier answer mistake permanent codes for correct codes: `check_redirects()` flags every 302/303/307 without determining whether the move is temporary, and accepts 301/308 without determining whether it is permanent. The reading also overstates “any chain”: the structured `redirect_chain` warning requires `total_hops > 1` and no detected loop.

CI-015.title: Eliminate 5xx Server Errors

entry_answer.why: A 5xx entry page is a server error on the site, and the crawl that finds the others never starts when the entry is one.

CI-015.reading: `summary.server_errors` counts crawled pages answering 500–599, the entry page among them; the site-wide 5xx the title names, over what the crawl reached. On an entry the audit could not read, `entry_answer` lets the entry's own request decide it: a 5xx answer fails it, anything else is NO_DATA.

CI-016.title: Provide Meaningful Image Alt Text
CI-016.reading: `alt_not_meaningful` counts images with no alt, a placeholder alt, or an empty alt where the image carries meaning: a link's only content or a large in-content image (F15: an empty alt never counted). Whether an alt describes its image is not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.qualifier: *Meaningful* is the placeholder signal: filenames, `image1`, `untitled` and the like do not count as descriptions.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and qualifier answer equate meaningfulness with avoiding recognized placeholders, but `alt_is_placeholder()` only checks length, patterns, and filename repetition. `inventory()` accepts unrelated descriptions and all empty alternatives without establishing whether the image is decorative, so zero `alt_not_meaningful` does not establish meaningful alt text.

CI-017.title: Validate HTML (W3C)
CI-017.reading: `summary.errors` is the W3C validator's error count for the served HTML.

shapes.conjunction: W3C names the validator, not a second subject.

CI-018.title: Analyze Logs & Manage Crawl Budget
CI-018.reading: `issues` holds server_log_audit's findings over a supplied log: waste, server errors and redirects served to search bots, disallowed and parameterised paths crawled, sitemap URLs never crawled. Whether crawl budget is managed is not decided, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Analysing the log is the means; crawl-budget findings are what the rule grades.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and conjunction answer overstate selected crawl diagnostics as deciding crawl-budget management: `_findings()` applies thresholds and inventory comparisons without establishing that budget is managed. The reading's “bot share” is also unsupported as an asserted finding; `_rates()` reports request totals, while `issues` contains the specific conditions emitted by `_findings()`.

CI-019.title: Noindex System & Search Pages (/search, /cart, /checkout, /login)
CI-019.reading: `indexable_urls` lists which of /search, /cart, /checkout, /login exist and are indexable when fetched (0.20 repair).

shapes.conjunction: The parenthetical lists the paths the rule requests.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `test_paths()` skips probes for paths blocked for every agent, allowing PASS without establishing the noindex directive requested by the title. The reading also overstates `indexable_urls`: failed probes are omitted into `unprobed_urls`, and `probe_url()` establishes only response status and detected noindex, not indexability generally. The conjunction answer correctly identifies the requested paths but does not address these gaps.

MS-020.title: Keep Page Titles Concise (Avoid SERP Truncation)
MS-020.reading: `title` is the document's title (the first outside SVG, whitespace collapsed), at most `article_seo.TITLE_MAX_CHARS`, 65, what the calibration fits into the 600 px desktop title for ordinary text; rendered width is not measured, and `measures` says so (F15: the registry wrote 60).

shapes.conjunction: The parenthetical is the reason for the limit.

second_reading.dispute: The reading correctly calls the 60-character limit a proxy, but that limitation contradicts its `answers` verdict. `title_tag.get_text(strip=True)` supplies text for a character-count assertion, which does not determine rendered width or SERP truncation; calling the parenthetical a reason does not establish that outcome.

MS-021.title: Avoid Overly Short Titles (<30 Characters)
MS-021.reading: `title` length at least 30 characters, the number the title states.

shapes.conjunction: The parenthetical is the threshold.

MS-022.title: Remove Duplicate Page Titles (Handle Canonical/Pagination Correctly)
MS-022.reading: `summary.duplicate_title_groups` counts titles shared by indexable crawled pages, a numbered page (`?page=2`) its own page and a noindex or canonicalised page left out (F15). Titles Google rewrites are not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Canonical is handled by exclusion; pagination is not recorded by the crawl, which the script says.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `_snippet_grouping_pages()` excludes pages declaring another canonical without checking whether that canonical is correct, and it does not recognize pagination. The conjunction answer acknowledges that pagination is unmeasured rather than showing how the rule answers that part of the title; `site_crawl.page_key()` also collapses query-based pagination.

MS-023.title: Detect & Resolve Keyword Cannibalization
MS-023.reading: `summary.cannibalized_queries` counts Search Console queries classified cannibalised or contested between two or more of the site's pages.

shapes.conjunction: Detecting is what the rule does; resolving is the fix.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict treats query splitting as established cannibalization, although `cannibalized_all` counts every non-branded spread with at least two logical page groups, including widely separated rankings without evidence of harmful competition. The conjunction answer names resolution as a fix but does not show that the asserted count verifies resolution; `analyze()` measures the same impression-sharing pattern before or after any fix.

MS-026.title: Ensure Every Page Has a Title
MS-026.reading: `summary.missing_title_pages` counts crawled HTML pages answering 200 whose title is absent or blank, noindex pages included; every page the crawl reached.

second_reading.dispute: The claim “every page the crawl reached” is false: `pages_from_inventory()` discards rows without `text_hash`, which `_read_page()` leaves unset when body text after chrome removal is empty, including successfully read HTML pages without titles. `carries_content()` also accepts content-bearing 2xx responses beyond 200. I therefore disagree with `answers`: `missing_title_pages` can omit a missing title on a page the crawl read.

MS-028.title: Fill Missing Meta Descriptions (High-Value Pages First)
MS-028.reading: `meta_description` present and not empty or whitespace (F15: whitespace was truthy). *High-Value Pages First* is an order of work no single page shows, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: *High-value pages first* is an order of work, not a second subject.

second_reading.dispute: `parse_html()` assigns the raw description `content`, so whitespace-only content satisfies truthiness. Although “high-value pages first” describes an order of work, the rule neither identifies those pages nor checks that order, leaving the `answers` verdict unsupported.

MS-029.title: Eliminate Duplicate Meta Descriptions
MS-029.reading: `summary.duplicate_description_groups` counts descriptions shared by indexable, self-canonical pages.

second_reading.dispute: The reading omits the body-content prerequisite: `pages_from_inventory()` excludes rows without `text_hash`, so `duplicate_descriptions()` never compares descriptions on successfully read HTML pages whose stripped body text is empty. I disagree with `answers` because duplicate descriptions on those pages can remain undetected, with no measures sentence disclosing the restriction.

MS-030.title: Keep Meta Descriptions ~150–160 Characters (Clear & Relevant)
MS-030.reading: `meta_description_band` is the description's length, whitespace collapsed, against article_seo's 100 and 144: 144 is what the calibration fits into the desktop snippet, so the title's 150–160 is cut and fails; under 100 fails; no description is MS-028's (0.120.0; it read 120–165 written into the registry). *Clear & Relevant* is not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: *Characters* is the band; *Clear & Relevant* has no reader, which `measures` states.
shapes.qualifier: *Clear* and *relevant* are judgements about the text, which the rule does not make; `measures` states it.

second_reading.dispute: The numeric reading is correct, but the `measures` verdict overlooks the sentence's attribution of the 100–144 band to snippet calibration. `article_seo.py` explicitly identifies `META_MIN_CHARS = 100` as editorial convention rather than a result measured from glyph widths, so that explanation is not fully accurate.

MS-031.title: Do Not Use Meta Keywords
MS-031.reading: `meta_keywords` is every keywords tag's non-empty content, joined, `None` when the page has no such tag; the rule passes on `None` or an empty value (F15: each tag overwrote the last) and is undecided when the output has no `meta_keywords` key at all.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overlooks how the meta-tag loop repeatedly overwrites `meta_keywords`. A populated keywords tag followed by an empty one leaves a falsy asserted value and passes despite the page containing populated meta keywords.

MS-032.title: Implement & Validate Structured Data (Where Relevant)
MS-032.reading: `summary.errors` is schema_required_props' count of missing required properties, applicable where nodes exist.

shapes.conjunction: Implemented is the applicability gate; validated is the assertion.
shapes.qualifier: *Where relevant* is `applies_when schema_nodes > 0`.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overstates validation: `has_value()` checks presence and nonemptiness, so `summary.errors == 0` does not establish valid structured data. The reading also omits malformed JSON-LD blocks, which `validate_schema_required_props()` counts as errors. The shape answers conflate existing typed nodes (`schema_nodes > 0`) with relevance; that gate cannot establish whether relevant structured data has been implemented.

MS-033.title: Add Social Preview Tags (Open Graph & Twitter Cards)
MS-033.reading: `score` is the share of Open Graph and Twitter Card checks the page passes; 80 is four in five.

shapes.conjunction: Both tag families feed the score.

second_reading.dispute: In `check_social_meta()`, `score` counts nonempty tag values, including optional tags; invalid values generate issues without losing points, so these are not checks the page necessarily passes. Although both families contribute, that does not establish the conjunction: eleven of thirteen tags pass the threshold even when `twitter:card` or a required Open Graph tag is missing, contradicting `answers`.

CN-034.title: Ensure Readable Font Sizes
CN-034.reading: `text_nodes_below_12px` counts visible elements with over three characters of their own text under 12px; shorter text and text directly in `<body>` are not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.qualifier: *Readable* is operationalised as the 12px floor.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overstates coverage: `small++` counts elements matching `body *` with a direct text node longer than three trimmed characters and computed font size below 12px, rather than all rendered text nodes. Calling readability a 12px floor does not address the excluded short text, text directly inside `body`, or whether that floor establishes readability.

CN-035.title: Make Hyperlinks Clear and Distinct
CN-035.reading: `links_indistinct` counts links in running text with no underline, weight or background of their own, in the text's colour or under 3:1 against it (F15: only `p/li/td/article a` and exact colour equality were read); a colour outside rgb() is counted unmeasured and withholds the zero, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Clear and distinct are one property: a link must look like a link.
shapes.qualifier: Read as visual distinctness from body text.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overstates the browser snippet: it scans only `p a, li a, td a, article a` and accepts any computed color difference, however imperceptible. Its comparison is against the immediate parent's styles, and it never assesses anchor clarity; redefining “clear and distinct” as this limited styling test does not answer the qualifier.

CN-036.title: Ensure Sufficient Text Contrast
CN-036.reading: `text_nodes_below_contrast` counts text below WCAG AA against its composited background colours; text over a CSS background image or gradient, or in a colour outside rgb(), is counted as unmeasured and withholds the zero (F15: it was scored against the colour behind the image), and `measures` says so.

shapes.qualifier: *Sufficient* is WCAG AA's ratio.

second_reading.dispute: The snippet excludes elements without their own text longer than three trimmed characters, while `bgOf()` ignores background images and gradients and the luminance calculation does not composite alpha. Naming WCAG AA thresholds answers which ratio is used, but these computation gaps mean zero does not establish sufficient contrast for the page's text.

CN-038.title: Balance Evergreen and Fresh Content
CN-038.reading: `score` is freshness_checker's recency of this page's dates and statistics; the site-level balance the title asks about is not measured.

shapes.conjunction: Evergreen and fresh across a site is out of reach for a one-page script; `measures` says so.

CN-039.title: Eliminate Low-Value/Thin Pages
CN-039.reading: `summary.thin_pages` counts crawled indexable pages under the word threshold.

shapes.conjunction: Low-value and thin are one subject, measured by length.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `detect_duplicates()` tests only whether retained, non-noindex pages fall below a word-count threshold, not whether their content has low value. The conjunction answer merely asserts that length measures both concepts; no computation establishes that relationship, and `pages_from_inventory()` even excludes pages with no remaining body text.

CN-040.title: Publish an Up-to-Date Privacy Policy
CN-040.reading: `signals.privacy_links` lists links to a privacy policy; whether the policy is current is not read.

shapes.existential: One link to the policy is what publishing it looks like from the page.

CN-041.title: Eliminate Internal Duplicate Content
CN-041.reading: `summary.duplicate_content_findings` counts exact-copy groups and MinHash near-duplicate pairs among indexable canonical crawled pages; an exact copy fails, near-duplicates alone warn, a noindex or canonicalised copy is not counted (F15). Other sites are not compared, and `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: The reading incorrectly describes a page count: `summary.exact_duplicate_groups` is `len(exact_dupes)`, counting group records formed from normalized, chrome-stripped text hashes, including informational records involving noindex pages. I disagree with `answers` because separately computed near-duplicates never affect the assertion, while canonical handling does not remove exact groups from it.

CN-044.title: Provide a Clear, Easy-to-Find Contact Page
CN-044.reading: `signals.contact_links` lists links named or addressed as contact, in the page's languages, plus phone and email links (0.116.0; it read `trust_links`, where an About, Privacy or Terms link counted, so a page with no contact route passed). How clear the contact page is, is not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.existential: One route to the people behind the page is what providing one looks like from the page.
shapes.qualifier: *Easy-to-find* is read as linked from the audited page; *clear* is what `measures` says is not read.

CN-048.title: Use Hierarchical Headings and Semantic HTML
CN-048.reading: `issues` carries heading-level skips and a missing <main>; nav and footer absence are deliberately not faults.

shapes.conjunction: Both halves are read: the heading hierarchy and the one landmark every page needs.

second_reading.dispute: The reading accurately describes `_structure_issues()`, but I disagree with `answers`: consecutive nonempty heading levels and the presence of `<main>` do not establish semantic HTML usage. The conjunction answer substitutes one landmark’s presence for the semantic HTML half of the title; the source explicitly acknowledges that it does not check whether navigation content uses appropriate markup.

CN-051.title: Avoid Intrusive Interstitials (Especially on Mobile)
CN-051.reading: `overlays_covering_content` counts visible fixed or sticky elements covering at least a quarter of the viewport; whether they hide content or are intrusive is not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: *Especially on mobile* is MB-094's own item; this one reads the rendered page.

second_reading.dispute: The source counts visible fixed or sticky elements whose viewport intersection occupies at least 25% of its area (`covered / area >= 0.25`), without checking whether they cover content or are intrusive interstitials. It also contains no load-timing requirement; referring mobile coverage to MB-094 does not resolve these gaps, so I disagree with `answers`.

CN-054.title: Ensure Lazy-Loaded Content Is Discoverable
CN-054.reading: `summary.lazy_lcp_candidates` counts images whose only source is JavaScript-deferred (data-src, data-srcset) with no native src, srcset or picture source (F15: data-srcset-only images were skipped); other lazy content is not read, and `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: The reading misstates the asserted computation: `inventory()` assigns `summary.lazy_lcp_candidates` the count of rows with `deferred_source` and no native `discoverable` source, without testing `loading` or `likely_lcp_candidate`. The `answers` verdict also overlooks non-image lazy-loaded content and `data-srcset`-only images discarded by the empty-`src` guard.

CN-056.title: Show Publication and Updated Dates
CN-056.reading: `date_signals.shown` requires a publication and an update date from declared sources; publication alone warns (0.112.0).

shapes.conjunction: Both halves are read.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict mistakes date detection for visible display: `check_freshness()` sets `date_signals.shown` from parseable source values, including metadata and JSON-LD, without checking visibility. “Declared sources” also overstates the semantics: `_time_dates()` accepts untyped `<time>` values, and two distinct dates suffice to infer an update. “Both halves are read” therefore does not establish that publication and updated dates are both shown as such.

CN-057.title: Show Author and Publisher Clearly
CN-057.reading: `signals.authorship` requires both an author and a publisher signal.

shapes.conjunction: Both halves are read, as a two-key object.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overlooks “Clearly”: `page_author_names()` accepts metadata and JSON-LD, and `_publisher_names()` accepts organisation nodes and `og:site_name`, without requiring visible identification. The conjunction answer correctly describes the two-key object, but both booleans being true does not establish that readers are clearly shown both parties.

CN-065.title: Use a Clear H1 Per Page
CN-065.reading: `h1` must hold exactly one non-empty heading; *clear* is read as that and nothing more.

shapes.qualifier: Exactly one non-empty H1; `measures` says the word means no more here.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict confuses a count with structural use: the headings loop merely appends every nonempty H2’s text, and `len_gte: 2` tests their number. It neither establishes that those headings organize content nor permits an appropriately structured page with only one H2.

CN-068.title: Strengthen Authorship & E-E-A-T Signals
CN-068.reading: `score` is eeat_signal_checker's weighted sum of an author, credentials, first-hand experience, policy and trust links, and external citations.

shapes.conjunction: Authorship is part of the E-E-A-T score, not a separate subject.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict is unsupported because `check_eeat()` awards points for vocabulary matches and links, without establishing the qualities those signals suggest. Its additive score can reach 36 from policy links, trust links, and three external links with no author, so saying authorship is “part of” the score does not answer whether the rule requires the title’s authorship condition.

KW-070.title: Own Your Branded Query (Homepage Ranks #1)
KW-070.reading: `branded.homepage_ranks_first` is true when the page Google serves most for the site's most-searched branded query is the homepage (the root, or a locale alternate of it) and averages position 1.5 or better. Branded means the query carries a name the operator supplied with `--brand` or the homepage publishes — `WebSite`/organisation `name` and `alternateName`, `og:site_name` — in any word order (0.122.0; it had judged the highest-click query, which on a site with a generic head term is not its name). `branded.searched` false — nobody searched the name — is N/A; no name at all is NO_DATA.

shapes.conjunction: *Own your branded query* is the homepage being the page served for it; *homepage ranks #1* is that page averaging position 1.5 or better. `homepage_ranks_first` is both.

second_reading.dispute: The reading describes the predicate substantially correctly, but its `answers` verdict equates an average position up to 1.5 with “Homepage Ranks #1.” Moreover, `find_branded()` evaluates `owns and first` for the highest-impression group, so a homepage averaging position 1 can fail when another group has more impressions. The conjunction answer repeats these substitutions rather than establishing the title's claim.

KW-071.title: Is there evidence of keyword duplication or overuse?
KW-071.reading: `summary.contested_queries` counts Search Console queries in the contested bucket: two or more of the site's pages ranking for one query.

second_reading.dispute: The reading omits essential conditions: `contested_all` excludes branded queries, requires at least two positioned logical page groups, and limits their position spread to three, after `find_query_spreads()` filters out rows below ten impressions. More fundamentally, its `answers` verdict mistakes nearby rankings for keyword duplication or overuse; neither function examines keyword usage or duplicated copy.

KW-076.title: Include the Primary Keyword in Body Copy
KW-076.reading: `keyword_usage.in_body` is whether the supplied primary keyword occurs in the body copy.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and reading equate the extracted corpus with body copy, but `main()` builds `full_text` only from H1–H3 headings and paragraphs collected by `extract_content()`. Keyword occurrences solely in lists, tables, or ordinary div text are excluded, so body-copy inclusion can still produce FAIL.

BL-081.title: Keep Anchor Text Natural and Varied
BL-081.reading: `summary.unnatural_anchor_targets` counts internal-link targets with exact-match overuse, low diversity, or an empty or generic anchor (F15). Anchors of other sites' links are not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Natural and varied are one property, read as anchor diversity per target.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and conjunction answer overstate the rule: `audit_anchor_text()` asserts only targets with at least five identical normalized editorial anchors constituting at least 80% of their nonempty editorial anchors, after excluding inferred navigation. It separately computes low diversity, empty anchors, and generic anchors without asserting them, so the rule does not establish either naturalness or general variety.

BL-083.title: Fix Broken Backlinks (Redirect or Update Link)
BL-083.reading: `targets.broken_count` counts pages other sites link to (the Links export's top linked pages) that now answer 4xx or not at all (0.107.0).

shapes.conjunction: The parenthetical is the fix; a redirected target is not counted as broken.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overstates what target status establishes about repaired backlinks. `_check_linked_pages()` counts all statuses >= 400, including 5xx, but counts unanswered requests only for `DEAD_FETCH_ERROR_KINDS`; other unanswered requests enter `unchecked`. The conjunction answer is also incorrect: a redirected target still counts as broken when its final response meets the failure condition.

BL-084.title: Check for Unnatural Link Concentration from Single Domains
BL-084.reading: `concentration.top1_share_pct` is the share of links from the single largest linking domain.

second_reading.dispute: `analyze()` uses `sites[0]["count"]`, without sorting or finding the maximum, so the asserted share is not necessarily the largest domain's share. Even when the export is ordered, the 50% threshold establishes concentration rather than unnaturalness, leaving the `answers` verdict unsupported.

BL-086.title: Track Total Backlinks (Quality Over Quantity)
BL-086.reading: `total_links` is the link count in the Links export; the rule can only say there are none, since tracking happens over time and quality is BL-084's and BL-087's.

shapes.conjunction: *Quality over quantity* is advice about reading the number; `measures` says what is read.
shapes.existential: At least one backlink; the count itself is reported, not judged.
shapes.qualifier: Quality is not read here; `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: The `measures` verdict overlooks that `total_links` sums counts, whereas the measures sentence describes listed-site presence; `parse_sheet()` accepts zero-count rows, so those conditions can disagree. The existential answer incorrectly says the count is not judged: `gte: 1` directly judges it. The qualifier answer says the measures sentence discloses the absence of quality assessment, but that sentence only discloses the absence of tracking over time; BL-084 and BL-087 do not establish quality either.

BL-087.title: Track Total Linking Root Domains
BL-087.reading: `linking_domains` counts distinct linking root domains in the export, at least 5.

second_reading.dispute: `analyze()` assigns `linking_domains = len(sites)`, without deduplicating names or extracting root domains, so the claim that it counts distinct linking root domains is unsupported. Requiring five parsed rows also does not establish tracking of the total, making the `answers` verdict too broad.

MB-093.title: Ensure Responsive Layout (Mobile-First)
MB-093.reading: `viewport` is the declared viewport meta; whether the layout fits a phone is MB-107's, which renders it.

shapes.conjunction: Mobile-first is the reason; the declared viewport is what is read.

MB-094.title: Avoid Intrusive Interstitials on Mobile
MB-094.reading: `mobile_overlays_covering_content` is CN-051's count from a phone-width render; whether the elements hide content or are intrusive is not read, and `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: `read()` supplies the phone-width gate, but the underlying `overlays++` counts fixed or sticky rectangles occupying at least 25% of the viewport, without establishing content obstruction or intrusion. The reading therefore overstates what the metric computes, and the `answers` verdict is unsupported.

MB-095.title: Keep Mobile Page Weight Light
MB-095.reading: `page_weight` bands Lighthouse's `total-byte-weight` from PageSpeed's mobile run — the bytes of every resource the page requested, scripts' own requests included: below 1,600 KiB, Lighthouse's documented target, passes; up to 5,000 KiB, where Lighthouse flags a payload, warns; above fails (0.119.0; it counted images over 250 KB and allowed five, and never totalled the page).

MB-096.title: Use Responsive Images
MB-096.reading: `large_without_srcset_count` counts images wider than 1280px, read from their own bytes, whose candidate set a phone ends up with has no width descriptors and no `max-width` `<source>` comes before it (F15: a density srcset or a format-only source counted as responsive); the widths offered are not read, and `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overstates what `audit()` establishes: `large_without_srcset_count` checks only fallback images wider than 1280px, and `responsive` means merely that an img or picture source has a nonempty srcset. It does not establish usable responsive choices, and smaller images never enter the asserted count.

MB-097.title: Optimize Image Formats & Compression
MB-097.reading: `legacy_or_heavy_count` counts large images with no WebP/AVIF offer plus any image over 250 KB (0.108.0); compression under 250 KB and the format of smaller images are not judged, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Formats and compression are each a half of the count.
shapes.qualifier: *Optimize* is read as those two halves.

second_reading.dispute: The count description is substantially accurate, but the `answers` verdict and qualifier answer equate optimization with two proxies. In `audit()`, an image can pass while poorly compressed below 250,000 bytes, and legacy formats are counted only when `row["large"]` is true; neither half establishes the corresponding optimization claim.

MB-098.title: Serve Properly Sized Images
MB-098.reading: `srcset_without_sizes_count` counts images whose width-described srcset has no sizes; a density (1x, 2x) srcset needs none, and an oversized image with no srcset is MB-096's.

second_reading.dispute: The reading omits `_needs_sizes()`, which restricts `srcset_without_sizes_count` to width-descriptor srcsets lacking sizes; density-descriptor srcsets without sizes pass. Consequently, the measures sentence's claim about every srcset is inaccurate, so the `measures` verdict is unsupported.

shapes.conjunction: *(see UX)* points at the UX items; it is not a subject.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and description as “mobile usability findings” overstate `_static_checks()`, which checks a viewport substring and raw HTML patterns for widths and positioning without rendering. Desktop-only width declarations can fail while actual mobile interaction problems pass, so these findings do not decide whether mobile UX issues are fixed.

MB-102.title: Optimize Video for Mobile
MB-102.reading: `issues` carries video_schema_checker's mobile-relevant video findings, applicable only where videos exist.

shapes.qualifier: *Optimize* is read as the script's issue set.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and “mobile-relevant video findings” description are unsupported: `check_video_schema()` checks VideoObject metadata properties and formats, with no mobile playback, layout, or performance checks. Its `videos` count comes from `find_schema_nodes(documents, "VideoObject")`, so applicability means declared schema nodes exist, not that videos exist. Reading “Optimize” as whatever issues the script emits does not address whether those checks establish mobile optimization.

MB-103.title: Make Tap Targets Easy to Click
MB-103.reading: `tap_targets_below_48px` counts visible links, buttons, form fields and role=button elements under 48px either way at phone width; spacing, overlap and occlusion are not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.external: *Click* is the user's click, not search clicks; nothing external is asked.

second_reading.dispute: The snippet counts selected visible elements whose bounding rectangle has either dimension below 48 pixels; it does not establish usable click areas or test occlusion and overlap. The shape answer correctly distinguishes user clicks from search clicks, but that does not support the broader `answers` verdict about ease of clicking.

MB-104.title: Ensure Favicon Displays in Mobile SERPs
MB-104.reading: `favicon.grade` grades the declared icon as Google's favicon page does: declared, crawlable by Googlebot-Image with the home page open to Googlebot, an image, square and at least 8 px fails otherwise; larger than 48 px in a listed format passes. Whether it represents the brand is what `measures` says is not read.

second_reading.dispute: The `measures` verdict and claim that the icon is “crawlable by Googlebot-Image” overlook that `check()` applies the page origin’s robots.txt to the icon URL even when that URL has another origin. `robots_rules.allowed()` matches the supplied URL’s path against those supplied rules, so unrelated page-origin restrictions can fail an externally hosted icon; the measures sentence does not disclose this gap.

MB-105.title: Ensure Content, Meta & Directives Match Between Served and Rendered HTML
MB-105.reading: `diffs` lists differences between the served and the rendered HTML in title, description, the robots and googlebot directives (F15), canonical, and counts of H1s, internal links, schema blocks and words.

shapes.conjunction: Content, meta and directives are each compared.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and conjunction answer are unsupported: `summarize()` omits robots directives entirely and represents content through counts rather than content equality. `audit()` compares only those summary fields, so `diffs` can remain empty despite changed directives or different content with equal counts.

SP-107.title: Load Content Fast (Prioritize Above-the-Fold)
SP-107.reading: `above_fold.rating` is the worse of FCP and LCP, both from CrUX or, for a page CrUX has no sample of, both from Lighthouse; a pass needs both (F15: FCP alone was read). Resource priority is not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Above-the-fold priority is what FCP times.
shapes.qualifier: *Fast* is the FCP band.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `parse_pagespeed_response()` computes an FCP rating, which does not establish that above-the-fold content loads quickly or receives priority. The conjunction answer incorrectly equates above-the-fold prioritization with first contentful paint. The reading also overstates the fallback: Lighthouse supplies FCP only when `field_data_available` is false, not whenever CrUX lacks FCP specifically.

SP-108.title: Pass Core Web Vitals (Field Data)
SP-108.reading: `field_cwv.verdict` passes only when every graded Core Web Vital is good in CrUX field data and LCP and CLS are among them (F15: one good metric passed), and is absent when there is none.

shapes.conjunction: The parenthetical names the data source the rule requires.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `field_cwv_verdict()` restricts grading to metrics included in `present` and permits pass even when only one recognized, good metric is present. “Every graded Core Web Vital” accurately describes that subset, but does not establish sufficient coverage for an overall Core Web Vitals pass.

SP-109.title: Fix Common Speed Traps
SP-109.reading: `blocking_third_party_count` counts render-blocking third-party scripts, one common trap among several.

second_reading.dispute: The `measures` verdict overstates the count's correspondence to rendering blockers: `_is_third_party()` excludes protocol-relative script URLs, and `audit()` classifies any external non-module script without `async` or `defer` as blocking, including non-executable script types. The measures sentence does not disclose these gaps, so my verdict remains `owed`.

SP-110.title: Run a Comprehensive Speed Audit
SP-110.reading: `issues` carries render-blocking resources and critical request chains read from the HTML; the other speed checks are separate items.

second_reading.dispute: The reading describes everything collected rather than what decides the assertion: `audit()` assigns stylesheets only `info`, while parser-blocking external scripts receive the failing `error` or `warning` severities. With `fetch_css=False`, CSS import chains are also unread; the measures sentence therefore overstates the verdict's scope, and my verdict remains `owed`.

SP-111.title: Check Core Web Vitals (Desktop) in Search Console
SP-111.reading: `field_cwv.verdict` for the desktop strategy, from CrUX through PageSpeed Insights — the dataset the Search Console report is built from.

shapes.conjunction: Desktop is the strategy passed; Search Console is the report the same data feeds.

SP-112.title: Check Core Web Vitals (Mobile) in Search Console
SP-112.reading: `field_cwv.verdict` for the mobile strategy, from CrUX through PageSpeed Insights — the dataset the Search Console report is built from.

shapes.conjunction: Mobile is the strategy passed; Search Console is the report the same data feeds.

SP-113.title: Meet Core Web Vitals Thresholds
SP-113.reading: `field_cwv.verdict` on mobile field data: every graded Core Web Vital within Google's good thresholds, LCP and CLS required (F15), INP when CrUX has it.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: the `present` comprehension in `field_cwv_verdict()` excludes missing metrics, and the final pass branch requires no minimum coverage. Every graded metric being good therefore does not establish that the page meets the Core Web Vitals thresholds comprehensively.

SE-114.title: Run Malware & Security Checks
SE-114.reading: `safe_browsing.threats` is Google Safe Browsing's threat list for the URL, required empty.

shapes.conjunction: Malware and security are both what Safe Browsing reports.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and conjunction answer overstate the lookup's scope: `check_safe_browsing()` returns Google's matches for the submitted URL across `SB_THREAT_TYPES`, not a general security assessment. An empty threat list does not establish that the site's malware and security checks are satisfied.

SE-115.title: Enable HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security)
SE-115.reading: `hsts_enabled` needs HTTPS and a positive max-age (0.112.0).

shapes.conjunction: The parenthetical expands the acronym.

SE-116.title: Ensure No Hacked Content or Malware

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict is unsupported: `check_safe_browsing()` derives `threats` from the API's `matches`, without inspecting content for hacking or independently detecting malware. Requiring those matches to be empty does not ensure the absence of hacked content or malware.

SE-117.title: Force HTTPS Across the Site (Single Canonical Protocol)
SE-117.reading: `http_to_https` is the worst answer the http:// address gave, asked of the audited page and up to three same-site pages it links to: a 301/308 to https passes, a 302/303/307 or nothing listening warns, and a page, an error, a loop or an http-only chain over plain HTTP fails; a broken connection withholds the verdict (0.118.0; it read `https`, the scheme the audited URL ended on, and never asked http://). The rest of the site is not requested, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: *Force HTTPS* is the http:// address redirecting; *single canonical protocol* is that redirect being permanent, which Google reads as a strong canonical signal and a temporary one as weak.

SE-118.title: Maintain a Valid TLS Certificate (HTTPS)
SE-118.reading: `valid` is True only after a verifying TLS handshake: unexpired, trusted, issued for the hostname.

shapes.conjunction: The parenthetical names the protocol.
shapes.qualifier: *Valid* is the handshake's own verdict.

SE-119.title: Make Cookie Banners Lightweight (No CLS)
SE-119.reading: `metrics.CLS.rating` is the page's layout shift as a whole; the cookie banner is not identified.

shapes.conjunction: *(No CLS)* names the metric read; the banner is what `measures` says is not isolated.

SE-120.title: Harden Security Headers (CSP, Permissions-Policy, Referrer-Policy)
SE-120.reading: `hardening_missing` lists which of CSP, Permissions-Policy and Referrer-Policy are absent (0.112.0).

shapes.conjunction: The three headers the title names are exactly the three read.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `check_security_headers()` computes `hardening_missing` solely from header names, so empty, invalid or unrestricted policies can pass. Reading all three named headers answers the conjunction shape, but their presence alone does not establish that they harden security.

IN-121.title: Configure Geo-Targeting Signals
IN-121.reading: `checks.x_default.passed` is whether the hreflang set carries exactly one x-default; region codes and country domains are not read.

IN-122.title: Implement Valid hreflang (With Return Tags)
IN-122.reading: `checks.return_tags.verified_and_valid` requires every alternate to link back, fetched and checked.

shapes.conjunction: Return tags are the validity condition the rule reads.
shapes.qualifier: *Valid* is return tags verified and codes valid.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overlooks that the configured arguments omit `--verify-returns`: `run_hreflang_check()` therefore leaves `verified_and_valid` absent, producing no verdict. The qualifier answer claims codes must be valid, but `check_lang_codes()` populates a separate field that this assertion never reads. The conjunction answer consequently leaves the title’s broader validity requirement unanswered.

IN-123.title: Make Page Language Obvious
IN-123.reading: `lang` is the html lang attribute, required present.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict equates a declaration with making the language obvious. `result["lang"] = html_tag.get("lang")` and the truthiness assertion accept any nonempty value without checking its validity or agreement with the page’s language.

IN-127.title: Use a Clear International URL Structure
IN-127.reading: `checks.url_structure.passed` requires locale URLs to use one of Google's supported structures — ccTLD, subdomain or subdirectory (0.26).

shapes.qualifier: *Clear* is one supported structure, not parameters.

IN-128.title: Serve the Correct Localized Page
IN-128.reading: `checks.self_reference.passed` is whether the page lists itself in its hreflang set; which version a visitor is served is not tested.

shapes.qualifier: *Correct* is not tested; `measures` says what is.

GO-131.title: Install & Configure Google Analytics 4
GO-131.reading: `measurement_ids` lists GA4 measurement IDs configured on the page.

shapes.conjunction: Install and configure are both read as a configured ID.
shapes.existential: One configured property is an installed GA4.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and both shape answers equate a matching ID with installation and configuration. In `check()`, `measurement_ids` includes `RE_GTAG_SRC` loader matches even without a configuration call, and neither regex establishes execution or correct configuration.

GO-132.title: Prevent GA4 Tag Duplication
GO-132.reading: `duplicates` lists GA4 IDs configured more than once.

second_reading.dispute: The reading incompletely describes `duplicates`: `check()` also appends repeated loader IDs and GTM container IDs appearing more than twice, rather than only GA4 IDs configured repeatedly. The `answers` verdict overstates these HTML counts, which cannot detect duplicate GA4 tags configured inside GTM or injected at runtime.

GO-134.title: Resolve Search Console Issues
GO-134.reading: `issues` carries errors and warnings Search Console reports against submitted sitemaps (0.23).

second_reading.dispute: The computation described is accurate, but the `answers` verdict is too broad: `detect_issues()` reads only submitted sitemap errors and warnings. Their absence does not establish that Search Console issues generally are resolved.

GO-135.title: Use URL Inspection & Rendered HTML
GO-135.reading: `issues` carries URL Inspection's findings for the audited URL — coverage, canonical, robots, indexing state. The API returns no rendered HTML, and `measures` says that half is not read.

shapes.conjunction: URL Inspection is read; rendered HTML is what `measures` says is not.

GO-136.title: Provide Clean XML Sitemaps
GO-136.reading: `issues` carries sitemap_checker's hygiene findings, robots conflicts included since 0.110.0.

shapes.qualifier: *Clean* is no finding at medium or above.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `_sitemap_entries()` silently skips `<url>` entries missing `<loc>` and accepts an unrecognized root containing a `<url>` child as a `urlset`, allowing malformed sitemap structures to pass. The qualifier answer defines “Clean” as absence of emitted findings without establishing that those findings cover sitemap cleanliness.

GO-137.title: Reconcile Indexed Pages vs. Sitemaps
GO-137.reading: `summary.unreconciled` counts sitemap URLs Google has not indexed plus indexed pages no sitemap lists (0.106.0).

shapes.conjunction: Indexed pages and sitemaps are the two sets compared.

second_reading.dispute: The reading overstates the second set as “indexed pages”: `_search_analytics_pages()` retrieves pages returned by Search Analytics for a historical period, not every currently indexed page. `analyze()` also inspects only a bounded prefix of sitemap URLs, and `page_key()` merges query variants. The conjunction answer names the intended sets without addressing these differences, so it does not justify `answers`.

GO-138.title: Remove Invalid URLs from Sitemaps
GO-138.reading: `invalid_url_count` counts listed URLs answering 400 or more, redirecting, noindex, or disallowed for Googlebot (0.110.0).

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`, and the reading overstates “noindex”: `invalid_urls` checks only `"noindex" in meta_robots.lower()`, ignoring `X-Robots-Tag`, `meta_googlebot`, and the `none` directive. Consequently, a listed URL excluded from indexing through those directives can contribute zero to `invalid_url_count` and permit PASS.

GO-139.title: Monitor & Improve Brand SERPs
GO-139.reading: `branded.ranks_first` is the site's own page ranking first — average position 1.5 or better — for its most-searched branded query, identified as KW-070's is (0.122.0; it had been the highest-click query). The rest of the brand results page is not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: *Monitor* and *improve* are one reading: the brand query's ranking over the Search Console window, which is what monitoring it shows and what improving it moves.

second_reading.dispute: The `measures` verdict overlooks that `find_branded()` tests only `owner = pages[0]`, the highest-impression logical page group, rather than whether any site page ranks first as the measures sentence claims. Its `0 < owner["position"] <= 1.5` predicate can fail while another group averages position 1. The conjunction answer also substitutes a ranking measurement for evidence of monitoring and improvement; the script computes neither activity nor change over time.

GO-143.title: Complete Every WebSite Node Google Reads for the Site Name
GO-143.reading: `incomplete_nodes_by_type.WebSite` counts WebSite nodes missing a property Google reads for the site name.

shapes.qualifier: *Complete* is every property Google documents for the site name.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and reading misidentify the count: `validate_schema_required_props()` marks a WebSite node incomplete for any missing required or recommended property across all its declared types, plus placeholders, including defects unrelated to site names. The qualifier answer is also inaccurate: the WebSite table checks `name` and `url`, omits the documented optional `alternateName`, and `has_value()` does not validate those properties' values.

GO-144.title: Optimize for Featured Snippets
GO-144.reading: `score` is answer_block_scanner's measure of question-and-answer blocks a snippet can lift.

shapes.qualifier: *Optimize* is read as answer-block readiness.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `scan_answer_blocks()` adds points for definitions, lists, and tables independently of question-and-answer blocks, so three qualifying tables alone pass with 36. The qualifier answer substitutes “answer-block readiness” for “Optimize” without establishing that the structural counts assess readiness or whether a snippet can lift the content.

GO-145.title: Optimize for AI Overviews & Zero-Click SERPs
GO-145.reading: `score` is citation_readiness for this one page — GEO-005's twin. Presence in AI Overviews or zero-click results is not observable here, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Neither surface is observed; `measures` names both.
shapes.external: AI Overview presence needs a source this audit does not have; `measures` says so.
shapes.qualifier: *Optimize* is read as citation readiness, and `measures` says that is all.

second_reading.dispute: The `measures` verdict treats `score` as establishing citation readiness, but `check_citation_readiness()` awards 15 points for an author signal and 10 for a canonical, meeting `gte: 25` without any citations. The sentence and qualifier answer therefore overstate what the rule decides; correctly acknowledging that neither search surface is observed does not cover this additional gap.

AR-146.title: Check Pagination
AR-146.reading: `pagination.issues` carries rel=prev/next pointing off-host or at the page itself, applicable only to a paginated page.

second_reading.dispute: The reading accurately describes `pagination.issues`, but I disagree with `answers`: `parse_html()` checks only whether the first declared prev/next targets are off-host or self-referential. Same-host, non-self targets pass without establishing correct pagination order or examining pagination controls.

AR-147.title: Use Short, Descriptive URLs
AR-147.reading: `rows.0.short` requires at most 115 characters, five path segments and two query parameters (0.115.0; it read `param_count` alone before, so a 300-character URL with no query passed). Whether the words describe the page is not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.qualifier: *Short* is the three bounds; *descriptive* is what `measures` says is not read.

AR-149.title: Eliminate Internal Redirects
AR-149.reading: `summary.internal_redirects` counts internal links that answer with a redirect in the crawl.

second_reading.dispute: `answers` overlooks that `summary.internal_redirects` counts fetched redirecting targets with `linked_from`, rather than checking every linked URL spelling. `site_crawl.page_key()` merges query and trailing-slash variants, and `crawl()` fetches only one spelling per key, allowing a redirecting variant linked from a read page to escape the count.

AR-150.title: Remove Redirect Chains and Loops
AR-150.reading: `total_hops` at most one on the entry URL's redirect walk.

shapes.conjunction: A loop is a chain with no end; both exceed one hop.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and conjunction answer are contradicted by `total_hops = max(0, len(result["chain"]) - 1)`: loop detection breaks before appending another entry, so a self-loop produces zero and a two-URL loop produces one. Both pass the assertion despite being loops; the rule tests the recorded count, not the unbounded length of a looping walk.

AR-151.title: Provide a Correct robots.txt
AR-151.reading: `correctness_problems` lists what stops the file saying what its owner means: an HTML page served at the path, more than the 500 KiB Google reads, a line that is not `field: value`, a directive no crawler reads, a rule before any user-agent, a relative sitemap, or the whole site disallowed for Googlebot; a 404 is the problem *no robots.txt* (0.117.0; it read `status` alone).

shapes.qualifier: *Correct* is the problem list: syntax a crawler parses, directives it reads, and not shutting Googlebot out.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and the claim that the check detects “the whole site disallowed” are unsupported: `correctness_problems()` calls `robots_rules.allowed()` only for `/`, so `Disallow: /$` triggers that problem while allowing other paths. Its syntax checks also accept an empty `User-agent:`, so the qualifier answer overstates what the problem list establishes; my verdict remains `owed`.

AR-152.title: Block Crawl Strategically with robots.txt
AR-152.reading: `user_agents` is truthy when robots.txt declares any user-agent group; whether its rules are strategic is a judgement the audit does not make.

AR-153.title: Design Clear Topic Hubs (Silos)
AR-153.reading: `score` is topical_cluster_mapper's score over topical clusters and their internal-link coverage, read since F06 over the pages the shared crawl read: a page's topic is its most frequent title word once the words more than half the titles share are set aside, and each topic's hub and spokes are expected to link both ways. The topic is a crude reading of a title, so the item answers whether pages that share a title word link to one another, not whether the site is designed in silos; a crawl cut at its caps withholds the score. A page whose title gives no readable word is a cluster of its own.

shapes.conjunction: *(Silos)* is another name for the hubs.
shapes.qualifier: *Clear* is read as the cluster score.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict contradicts the reading’s own admission that the rule does not decide whether the site is designed in silos. `map_clusters()` scores missing reciprocal links around a selected hub, and `score >= 70` permits seven missing links. Saying “Clear is read as the cluster score” does not explain how that computation establishes clarity.

AR-154.title: Optimize E-commerce Category Pages
AR-154.reading: `issues` carries collection_page_checker's category-page findings, applicable only where product links are detected.

shapes.qualifier: *Optimize* is read as the script's issue set.

second_reading.dispute: The qualifier answer defines “Optimize” as the issue set without showing that those issues establish optimization. `check_collection_page()` can satisfy the assertion through word quantity and H1/meta-description presence without checking their relevance or quality; its product-link and pagination findings are only `info`. Thus the reading describes the findings and applicability correctly, but its `answers` verdict is unsupported.

AR-155.title: Use Consistent, Descriptive URL Slugs
AR-155.reading: `rows.0.flags` must be empty: no uppercase, underscore, archive pattern, deep path, parameters or excess length; whether the words describe the page is not read.

shapes.qualifier: *Consistent* is the flag set; *descriptive* is what `measures` says is not read.

second_reading.dispute: The `measures` verdict overlooks that `analyze_urls()` checks uppercase letters only in `parsed.path`, whereas the measures sentence claims their absence throughout the URL. The shape answer also equates “consistent” with an empty flag set, but the assertion compares no slug conventions across pages.

AR-158.title: Implement Breadcrumbs (UI + Schema)
AR-158.reading: `breadcrumbs` requires both a BreadcrumbList schema with a trail entry and a detectable breadcrumb UI; a Microdata/RDFa trail counts as UI only with a link in it (F15: an empty list or carrier counted).

shapes.conjunction: Both halves are read, as a two-key object.

second_reading.dispute: The claim that both halves are independently established is unsupported: `_has_breadcrumb_ui()` immediately returns true when `_breadcrumb_markup()` finds a Microdata/RDFa BreadcrumbList carrier. Neither that carrier nor the JSON-LD type check requires populated breadcrumb entries, and UI markers do not establish a visible trail, so the `answers` verdict and conjunction answer overstate coverage.

AR-162.title: Strengthen Internal Links and Remove Orphans
AR-162.reading: `issues` carries link_profile's internal-link findings over the crawl, orphans included.

shapes.conjunction: Strengthening links and removing orphans are both issue types in the set.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`, and the conjunction answer treats an issue type as proof that “strengthening” is decided. `analyze_link_profile()` tests zero outgoing links and an average below three alongside orphans; `graph_from_inventory()` computes outgoing counts with `len(internal)`, including repeated and self-directed links. Those counts can satisfy the rule without establishing strong or relevant internal linking.

AR-163.title: Control Faceted Navigation (E-commerce)
AR-163.reading: `issues` carries faceted_nav_audit's findings on facet URLs that are neither canonicalised nor noindexed, applicable only where facets exist.

shapes.conjunction: *(E-commerce)* scopes the item; the applicability gate is facet presence.

second_reading.dispute: The reading omits `audit()`’s medium-severity `path_explosions` finding, which affects the assertion regardless of canonical/noindex controls. It also overstates “canonicalised”: any parsed canonical suppresses `facet_missing_canonical`, including a self-canonical retaining the facet parameters. The conjunction answer equates facet presence with the E-commerce scope, although `faceted_count` checks parameter names without establishing that the page is an e-commerce page.

TE-166.title: Add a Favicon
TE-166.reading: `favicon` is the first link whose rel names `icon` or `apple-touch-icon` (F15: `shortcut` alone counted). Whether the file loads is MB-104's, and `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: “The first declared icon link” overstates `seo_common.favicon_href()`, which also accepts a `shortcut` rel token alone without an `icon` token. Its truthy href establishes neither a working icon resource nor the absence of a favicon when no declaration exists, so the `answers` verdict is unsupported.

TE-167.title: Monitor Site Uptime

entry_answer.why: The item reads whether one request of this audit was answered below 500. When the entry request was not, the gate stopped the run on exactly that answer.

TE-167.reading: `uptime.reachable` is one request during the audit answered below 500; monitoring over time needs a service. On an entry the audit could not read, `entry_answer` lets the entry's own request decide it: a 5xx answer or no answer at all fails it, anything else is NO_DATA. Re-read at F06, when `requires` moved from `api` to `crawl`: the reading holds, and the item is now asked on a host only this machine reaches as well, since no third party is in its one request.

TE-168.title: Fix Broken & Redirected Links
TE-168.reading: `summary.broken_or_redirected` counts internal links that fail or redirect and external links that fail, site-wide over the crawl (0.107.0).

shapes.conjunction: Broken and redirected are both counted — an external redirect is not a defect; broken alone is the warn band.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and conjunction answer exclude external redirects without support from the title. `links_from_inventory()` records `external_redirected` but omits it from `summary.broken_or_redirected`, so “broken and redirected are both counted” is incomplete; calling external redirects harmless does not close that gap.

TE-169.title: Provide Internal Links in the Served HTML
TE-169.reading: `raw.internal_link_count` counts internal links in the served HTML, before JavaScript (renamed 0.53.0).

shapes.existential: The title asks that the served HTML carry internal links; one is the floor, and MB-105 compares served with rendered.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overstates what `raw.internal_link_count` establishes: `summarize()` uses `href.startswith()` against the page’s scheme and authority, allowing an external URL such as `https://example.com.evil/` to count for `https://example.com/`. The existential answer reasonably explains the threshold of one, but does not resolve this misclassification; MB-105 also compares link counts rather than establishing that the links are internal.

TE-170.title: Configure Server Rewrites & Headers
TE-170.reading: `issues` carries caching, compression and Vary findings on the page response; URL rewrite rules are not read.

shapes.conjunction: Headers are read; rewrites are what `measures` says are not.
Blocklist and Safe Browsing are the same lookup.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and conjunction answer assume coverage the source does not establish: `check_safe_browsing()` queries only `SB_ENDPOINT` and constructs `threats` from its response. The script supplies no separate blocklist evidence or basis for treating the title's two requested checks as equivalent.

TE-172.title: Implement Structured Data Correctly
TE-172.reading: `summary.errors` counts rich-results guard errors in the page's structured data, applicable where nodes exist.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overstates the check: `guard_rich_results()` counts JSON-LD parse failures, deprecated types, and missing properties from `missing_rich_result_props()`, whose table covers only four types. Zero errors does not establish correct structured-data implementation generally; `has_value()` accepts nonempty values without validating their meaning or correctness.

TE-174.title: Minify & Optimize CSS
TE-174.reading: `unminified_count` counts stylesheets the page loads that are not minified. Unused rules and critical-path CSS are not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Minify is read; the rest of optimize is what `measures` says is not.
shapes.qualifier: *Optimize* beyond minification is not read; `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: The `measures` verdict and reading overstate coverage: `check()` automatically marks files below `SMALL_FILE_BYTES` minified, examines only external stylesheet links, and can omit failed fetches from `unminified_count` without marking truncation. Larger fetched files are classified by `looks_minified()`'s structural heuristic, rather than a definitive minification test. The shape answers address the optimization gap but do not make the measures sentence's claim about “every stylesheet the page loads” accurate.

TE-175.title: Secure Pages & Eliminate Errors
TE-175.reading: `page_security` is what a browser does to the page: served over plain HTTP fails; over HTTPS, a script, stylesheet, frame, object or srcset requested over http:// is blocked and fails, an image or media file is upgraded and warns, nothing mixed passes — MDN's two kinds of mixed content (0.121.0; it counted missing security headers, SE-115's and SE-120's subject). URLs inside CSS and the page's other errors are not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: *Secure pages* is the page over HTTPS with nothing loaded over plain HTTP; *eliminate errors* is the mixed content a browser blocks, and the other errors are other items', which `measures` states.
shapes.qualifier: *Secure* is read as the browser's own test — the page's scheme and every load it makes — not as header coverage, which is SE-115 and SE-120.

second_reading.dispute: The claim that this checks “every load” or determines actual browser behavior exceeds the source: `mixed_content()` inspects selected HTML attributes without observing resource requests, and explicitly omits CSS URLs. The blanket claim that HTTP images and media are upgraded also misses its `ipaddress.ip_address()` branch, which classifies their `src` URLs as blockable when the hostname is an IP address.

TE-176.title: Fix Canonicalization Issues
TE-176.reading: `issues` carries canonical_checker's findings over every crawled HTML page: a missing or cross-host canonical, a canonical whose target does not answer 200, and a target that canonicalises elsewhere.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overlooks that `site_crawl._read_page()` retains only `parse_html()`’s first HTML canonical, so `check_inventory()` can pass conflicting declarations through its early `self_canonical` branch. The reading also inaccurately says targets must answer 200: the actual test is `carries_content(target_status)`, which accepts other content-bearing 2xx statuses. HTTP `Link` canonicals are absent from the inventory evidence this rule reads.

TE-177.title: Provide a Title Element in the Served HTML
TE-177.reading: `raw.title` is the title in the served HTML, before JavaScript (renamed 0.53.0).

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict and reading overlook that `parse_html()` uses `text_or_none(soup.find("title"))`, which takes nonempty text from the first matching element anywhere, including an SVG `<title>`. Consequently, `raw.title` can pass without an HTML document title, while an empty HTML title element fails despite being present.

TE-178.title: Audit Neighboring Sites on the Server

cannot_fail.why: check_neighbors() resolves the hosting IP and stops there.
