TE-178.reading: `neighbors.suspicious` is never fabricated: enumerating co-hosted sites needs a reverse-IP service, so the item is NO_DATA until one is wired in.

second_reading.dispute: The reading accurately acknowledges the missing computation but incorrectly awards `answers`. `check_neighbors()` resolves an IP and never emits `suspicious`, so the assertion always yields no verdict and never answers the neighboring-sites question.

TE-179.title: Review Domain Registration History

cannot_fail.why: 0.44.0 gave this item the domain-history half of its title through whois age: established passes, younger than 90 days warns, an absent age is NO_DATA. The warn band is the assertion's exact complement on purpose — a young domain is worth pricing, not a defect to fix — and the ruling that no 'worth knowing' status exists still stands. ROADMAP.md records the reasoning.

TE-179.reading: `whois.age_days` at least 90, a younger domain warning (renamed and ruled 0.101.0).

second_reading.dispute: The age-and-warning description is accurate, but the `answers` verdict is not. `check_whois()` selects the newest parsed creation date and computes `age_days`; comparing that age with 90 days does not review domain registration history, and no `measures` sentence covers the gap.

TE-180.title: Meet Accessibility (WCAG) Basics
TE-180.reading: `wcag_a_failures` counts the level-A failures the HTML shows — images without alt, form fields without an accessible name, no page language (0.117.0; it read a score in which two such failures passed and a non-WCAG H1 count cost the same). Contrast is CN-036's and keyboard use is not tested, and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: *(WCAG)* names the standard; its level-A criteria that static HTML shows are what is read.

second_reading.dispute: The `measures` verdict and claim to count fields “without an accessible name” exceed what `checker()` computes: a truthy `aria-labelledby` or an existing label suffices without resolving references or checking label text. The loop also skips all `image`, `button`, `submit`, and `reset` inputs without examining their actual names. Consequently, the conjunction answer’s claim to read the HTML-visible level-A criteria is too broad, and the measures sentence does not accurately cover these omissions.

TE-181.title: Validate the Rendered DOM (W3C)
TE-181.reading: `summary.errors` is the W3C validator's error count for the rendered DOM from the supplied artifact.

shapes.conjunction: W3C names the validator.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: the artifact producer captures `document.documentElement.outerHTML`, which omits the document’s doctype, and `validate()` submits that incomplete serialization to Nu. Although `summary.errors` counts Nu’s errors for the supplied artifact, a missing-doctype error can be introduced by this capture rather than exist in the rendered document.

MD-184.title: Confirm the Page References at Least One Image

check.entry_only: Whether the audited page references an image is a question about that page. A privacy or contact page with no picture is not a defect, and under the sample's worst-page rule it failed the exemplary fixture (0.49.0); so the entry page decides, and sampled pages do not.

MD-184.reading: `summary.images` is the number of images the entry page references by any source: src, data-src, srcset, a `<picture>` source or data-srcset (F15: srcset- and picture-only images were skipped). Since F06 it reads the descriptive count, written on every page read, rather than `count`, and `check.entry_only` keeps sampled pages from deciding it: the URL the operator asked about is the page the title means.

shapes.existential: The title itself says at least one.

second_reading.dispute: The existential shape answer is correct, but the `answers` verdict treats a restricted image count as complete: `parse_html()` derives `src` from `src` or `data-src`, and `inventory()` skips images lacking both. A valid `srcset`-only image therefore leaves `summary.images` at zero despite the page referencing an image; the supplied title does not restrict references to those counted attributes.

MD-185.title: Optimize Images
MD-185.reading: `issues` carries image_weight_audit's image findings, applicable where the page has images; a large image with no WebP/AVIF offer is a warning (F15: info), as an over-250 KB one is, so no image MB-097 fails passes here.

shapes.qualifier: *Optimize* is read as the script's issue set.

second_reading.dispute: The reading describes the issue list but overlooks which severities decide the assertion: `audit()` assigns missing srcset, missing required sizes, and legacy raster formats `info`, which the rule permits. The qualifier answer therefore does not justify `answers`: even the script's own image findings can remain present on PASS.

MD-186.title: Provide Meaningful Alt Text
MD-186.reading: `alt_not_meaningful`, CI-016's count: no alt, a placeholder alt, or an empty alt on a link's only content or a large in-content image (F15). Whether an alt describes its image is not read, and `measures` says so.

shapes.qualifier: *Meaningful* is the placeholder signal.

second_reading.dispute: The count description is accurate, but the `answers` verdict and qualifier answer incorrectly treat placeholder detection as deciding meaningfulness. `alt_is_placeholder()` cannot reject an unrelated description that avoids its patterns, and `inventory()` accepts empty alt text without determining whether the image is decorative.

MD-187.title: Fix Broken Images
MD-187.reading: `broken_image_count` counts crawled image URLs that answer dead, 404/410, a 204/205, or a 2xx declaring a type outside `image/*`; an untyped or octet-stream answer is read for an image header (F15: any non-text 2xx was fine).

second_reading.dispute: “Fail to load” overstates `_classify_image()`, which accepts ordinary 2xx/3xx responses unless they carry a text media type and does not validate image content. An empty 204 or corrupt bytes served as `image/png` can pass, so `broken_image_count == 0` does not establish that the crawled image references load successfully.

MD-189.title: Use Modern Formats & Responsive Images
MD-189.reading: `large_legacy_or_unresponsive_count` counts images wider than 1280px lacking a width-described srcset or media source, or a WebP/AVIF offer (F15: the owner ruled both halves asserted; only the responsive one was), and `measures` says so.

shapes.conjunction: Both halves are asserted per image, by the owner's ruling of 2026-11-08.

second_reading.dispute: The reading acknowledges that the assertion checks only the responsive half, contradicting its `answers` verdict for a title requiring modern formats and responsive images. In `audit()`, `large_without_srcset_count` never consults `modern_format`; pointing to MB-097 or invoking double counting does not answer this item's conjunction.

MD-190.title: Implement Video SEO Essentials
MD-190.reading: `issues` carries video_schema_checker's VideoObject findings, applicable only where videos exist.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict overstates what `check_video_schema()` establishes: its property-presence and format checks do not verify actual video accessibility, metadata accuracy, or broader video SEO essentials. The description of VideoObject findings is accurate, but “applicable only where videos exist” confuses the count of declared VideoObject nodes with actual videos.

LO-198.title: Implement Local Business Structured Data
LO-198.reading: `local_business_nodes` counts LocalBusiness nodes across the crawl.

shapes.existential: Implementing the data is one node carrying it.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `site_crawl._read_page()` obtains schema nodes from `parse_html()`, which extracts only JSON-LD, so LocalBusiness implemented through Microdata or RDFa can fail. The existential answer explains why one node suffices for presence, but does not cover this format limitation in the unrestricted title.

LO-200.title: Publish Complete NAP in LocalBusiness Data
LO-200.reading: `nap_complete` requires name, address and telephone in the LocalBusiness data.

shapes.qualifier: *Complete* is all three.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `check_local_seo()` computes `nap_complete` using only `node.get(prop)` truthiness for name, address and telephone. The qualifier answer equates complete NAP with three truthy properties, although an address containing only `{"@type": "PostalAddress"}` and whitespace name and telephone values passes without publishing complete NAP.

GEO-001.title: llms.txt present and well-formed
GEO-001.reading: `well_formed` is true when /llms.txt answers 200 with a `# ` title as its first line and is not an HTML page — the one element the format requires (0.115.0; it read `exists`, which any 200 satisfied). A 404 is false; any other status leaves it unset.

shapes.conjunction: Present and well-formed are both read: a 404 fails, and so does a 200 that is not an llms.txt file.

second_reading.dispute: The verdict stands, but the status description is inaccurate: `check_llms_txt()` parses every response accepted by `carries_content()`, which includes all 2xx statuses except 204, not just 200. Those responses can therefore set `well_formed` to true or false rather than leaving it unset.

GEO-002.title: llms.txt quality score
GEO-002.reading: `quality.score` is llms_txt_checker's structure and content score, at least 60.

shapes.qualifier: *Quality* is the score.

second_reading.dispute: I retain `owed`: `_score_quality()` awards points for structural presence, counts and character lengths without assessing whether the information is accurate or useful. The qualifier answer, “Quality is the score,” does not explain how those computations establish quality; a title, one-character description and one syntactically matched link already score the passing 60.

GEO-003.title: AI crawler policy is explicit
GEO-003.reading: `policy_grade` says which scopes robots.txt names in a group of their own — training and answer feeding, among tokens that honour robots.txt; a policy left to `*` names nothing.

second_reading.dispute: The reading accurately describes scope naming, but that narrower computation does not support `answers`. `matrix()` passes when just one training token and one answer-feeding token are named, while `robots_rules.group_for()` reports wildcard matches as `"*"`, so an explicit wildcard policy fails and policies leaving other crawlers implicit can pass.

GEO-004.title: Answer blocks present for AEO
GEO-004.reading: `score` is answer_block_scanner's answer-block readiness, GO-144's twin.

second_reading.dispute: I disagree with `answers`: `score` does not establish answer-block presence or readiness, because `scan_answer_blocks()` lets four qualifying lists pass with 40 even when `direct_answers` and `definitions` are empty. Conversely, one qualifying direct answer alone scores 20 and fails, so the threshold does not decide the title’s presence question.

GEO-005.title: Content is citation-ready for AI search

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict equates a weighted signal score with content citation readiness. In `check_citation_readiness()`, author and canonical presence alone supply the required 25 points, while `claim_coverage` compares aggregate citation counts with regex-matched claims without checking whether any source supports a claim.

GEO-006.title: Entity is resolvable (Wikidata / KG)
GEO-006.reading: `summary.sameas_missing_critical` counts critical entities with no sameAs to a knowledge base.

shapes.conjunction: Wikidata and the Knowledge Graph are the targets sameAs may name.

second_reading.dispute: `analyze_sameas()` counts missing platform names, not critical entities: its missing set includes Wikipedia, Wikidata, LinkedIn, and Twitter/X across pooled schema links. `run_entity_check()` copies that count into the asserted path without incorporating its Wikidata or Google Knowledge Graph lookup results, contradicting `answers`. The conjunction response also misidentifies the computation: Google Knowledge Graph is not a platform in `SAMEAS_PLATFORMS`, and mentioning possible link targets does not establish entity resolution.

GEO-007.title: IndexNow configured
GEO-007.reading: `key_valid` is whether the supplied IndexNow key file is served and matches.

second_reading.dispute: “Served and matches” overstates `check_key_file()`, which accepts any content-bearing response containing the key as a substring rather than requiring matching key-file contents. The `answers` verdict also overreaches: `key_valid` checks only that response, while submission through `ping_indexnow()` is optional and absent from the supplied arguments.

GEO-008.title: Snippet directives leave the page usable in AI answers and result snippets
GEO-008.reading: `rows.0.snippet_controls.snippet_availability` is full, limited or suppressed from meta and header snippet directives.

shapes.conjunction: AI answers and result snippets obey the same directives.

second_reading.dispute: The `answers` verdict confuses unrestricted availability with usability: `snippet_controls()` returns `limited` for a positive `max-snippet` or a partial `data-nosnippet` exclusion, which the assertion fails although usable content can remain. It also searches X-Robots-Tag without filtering crawler scopes, so another crawler's restriction can fail the item. The conjunction answer does not resolve either mismatch between the asserted classification and usability in both named contexts.

TECH-001.title: Modern schema types only (no HowTo/FAQ misuse)
TECH-001.reading: `summary.retired_types` counts the JSON-LD nodes whose type Google no longer shows a rich result for, HowTo and FAQPage among them, or shows only for some sites.

TECH-002.title: Font loading does not block render

Meanwhile, `audit()` emits failing warnings for missing preload `crossorigin` and stylesheet fetch failures, which do not establish rendering blockage; my verdict remains `owed`.

SP-214.reading: `lcp_ms` from the supplied local trace, at most 2500.

SP-215.reading: `cls` from the supplied local trace, at most 0.1.

MB-107.title: Page fits the phone viewport without horizontal scrolling
MB-107.reading: `horizontal_overflow_px` at most 1 at phone width in the rendered artifact.

MB-108.title: Text is not clipped or cut off at a phone width
MB-108.reading: `text_nodes_clipped` counts visible h1-h3, p, a, button and li whose scroll size exceeds their client size at phone width; a scrollable box counts and an ancestor's clip is not read, and `measures` says so.

second_reading.dispute: The `clipped++` condition measures scroll dimensions exceeding client dimensions for selected elements, without establishing that their text is cut off.
